import pandas as pd

# Read source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the first numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv('autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_6/training_0.csv', index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv('autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_6/training_1.csv', index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv('autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_6/training_2.csv', index_col=0)

# UNION Source5_6_0 and Source5_6_2 (same schema)
union_0_2 = pd.concat([source0, source2], ignore_index=True)

# JOIN union_0_2 with Source5_6_1 on 'state'
joined = pd.merge(union_0_2, source1, how='inner', on='state')

# Convert 'year' to integer if not already
joined['year'] = joined['year'].astype(int)

# Aggregate: group by 'state' and 'year'
# sum draw_sales, max full_state and pop (full_state is string in source1, but target expects integer - we will convert)
# full_state in source1 is string, target expects integer - this is suspicious, but target example shows integer 8 for all columns
# We will convert full_state to integer by mapping unique full_state strings to integers (ordinal encoding)
full_state_map = {v: i+1 for i, v in enumerate(joined['full_state'].unique())}
joined['full_state'] = joined['full_state'].map(full_state_map)

agg = joined.groupby(['state', 'year'], as_index=False).agg({
    'draw_sales': 'sum',
    'full_state': 'max',
    'pop': 'max'
})

# Ensure columns are in target schema order and types
agg = agg[['state', 'year', 'draw_sales', 'full_state', 'pop']]

# Convert draw_sales, full_state, pop to integer as target expects integer
agg['draw_sales'] = agg['draw_sales'].astype(int)
agg['full_state'] = agg['full_state'].astype(int)
agg['pop'] = agg['pop'].astype(int)

# Write output
agg.to_csv('autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_6/target_multisource_critique_history.csv', index=False)
